label: Flat
//: The look these apps wore before they spoke this language, restated as tokens - axibridge's palette carrying axiroster's relief, because the two were the same idea reached twice. A theme restates tokens and nothing else - see the Themes section of docs/RULES.md. This one is the cheapest a theme has been: unlike glass it costs the language no new token at all, because everything it wants to say - layered surfaces with a lit top edge, a hairline, a soft drop, a small corner - is something tokens.css already declares. The name is a hazard worth naming: package.json calls the main theme flat and outlined, and this theme is flat in the other sense, the one where nothing is outlined and nothing is blocked. What separates them is not flatness, it is the edge and the relief.
//surfaces: The stack is axibridge's - #090b10 page, #1a1f2e panel, #222838 the step above it - cooler and darker than the language's neutral slate, which is most of why the theme reads as a different app rather than a different accent. The gradient is axiroster's: it painted its page flat and gave every raised thing a two-stop top-to-bottom fade (linear-gradient(#232327, #202023)) so the surface caught light at its head and lost it at its foot. Ported here at the same ~4-unit spread around each of axibridge's flat values, which is why the panels read as lifted off the page rather than merely lighter than it. Safe because every surface token is consumed through the background shorthand, never background-color - the one token that is not, --axi-well-fill, stays a flat colour below. --axi-surface-float needs no restating: it defaults to var(--axi-surface), so a floating pane inherits the same fade for free. That is the whole of glass's float problem not arising - a pane at .42 alpha goes illegible when a table scrolls under it, and an opaque one never does.
//well: --axi-well-fill defaults to --axi-ground, on the reading that a hole in a panel shows the page. Both apps disagreed, and identically: axibridge's --bg-input and axiroster's panel.sunk were each their own step between the page and the panel rather than a return to the page. #141822 is axibridge's, kept flat rather than graded because the well is the one surface the language paints with background-color, where a gradient would simply fail to apply. The part that cannot be folded in is axiroster's shadow-sunk, inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, .45) - the language has four shadow tokens and none of them is the well's, so the well reads as cut one shade into the panel without also reading as pressed. --axi-well-line follows --axi-rule and needs nothing.
//edges: The outline becomes a hairline, and the three border steps all go to 1px. White at .10 and .07 rather than axibridge's .08 and .06: axiroster drew its lines as opaque greys (#2f2f34 on a #1a1a1c panel, a little over a tenth of a step of light) and its stronger #3a3a40 on inputs, so meeting it means lifting the line slightly. Translucent is the right spelling for both now that the surfaces are graded - a fixed grey would drift against the fade, where a white at alpha lights consistently from head to foot. This is the theme's whole answer to rule 3's outlined half: a panel one shade off its ground, fenced by a light hairline, reads as outlined without any ink in the outline.
//inks: The toll for relighting the line. --axi-ground-deep, --axi-accent-ink and --axi-ink-on-fill all default to var(--axi-ink-line), so lifting the line to translucent white would drag them with it and write near-invisible text on the gold button and the saturated chips. They are restated at axibridge's own #0c1015 for that reason alone - the ink a filled button writes in has not changed, it has only stopped being spelled as the outline. Glass pays this identical toll, which is a sign it belongs to the language rather than to any one theme.
//block: A soft drop instead of the hard offset, at axibridge's literal shadow values, each with axiroster's lit inner edge appended - inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, .05), the 1px highlight that sold its cards as floating. Rule 3 asks that a raised element read as raised; a 6px offset in near-black is the main theme's answer, and a drop plus a lit top edge is this one's. Glass spells its relief the same way, from the other direction. The hover variants deepen, lift, and brighten that edge rather than sliding further off, because there is no offset here to grow - axibridge lifted --border-hover and axiroster darkened its accent, neither of which a theme can spell, so the relief carries the state on its own.
//accent: Not restated, deliberately, exactly as glass does not restate it. axibridge's base accent was an electric blue #3b82f6 and axiroster's was an emerald #047857 - which is the argument by itself. Pinning either would make the theme and the accent picker fight over one token, and would pick a side between two apps this theme is trying to describe at once. A theme repaints the surface layer; the accent stays the app's to choose, and an app that sets none is gold under this theme as under every other.
//text: #e8eaed and #8b929e are axibridge's, within a shade of axiroster's #e9eaec and #9aa0a8 - further evidence the two looks were one look. --axi-text-faint is nobody's: axibridge's #4a5162 sits at about 2.2:1 on the panel and axiroster's #646a73 was the more legible of the two, and the language spends faint ink on eyebrows and captions - text, not decoration. #5d6577 is axibridge's colour walked up until it passes, landing near where axiroster already was, which is the one place this theme is deliberately unfaithful to what it is reproducing.
//scrim: The first thing the every-theme rule above caught. glass restates the scrim and flat did not, and inheriting the language's rgba(6, 7, 9, .72) was very nearly right - both grounds are a cool near-black - which is exactly what makes it the wrong kind of silence: the theme had not decided, it had been lucky. Flat's own ground is #090b10, so its scrim is that walked two steps down and held at the language's .72. What a scrim has to do is put a whole page behind a drawer without turning it grey, and a scrim mixed from a different palette than the page it covers is how a dimmed page picks up a cast.
//corner: Under both apps, and now under axibridge too on the panel. axiroster rounded generously - 12px cards, 8px buttons and fields, 6px chips - where axibridge held to 8/4/2; the first pass split them at 10/6/3 and the second sat on axibridge's own numbers at 8/5/2. 6/4/2 goes one step further: axibridge's control and chip radii exactly, with the panel brought under its 8px so a panel reads as squared-with-the-corner-knocked-off rather than as a card. That inverts the usual relation between the two steps - the panel's 6px and the control's 4px are close enough that a button inside a panel no longer reads as noticeably softer than it, which is the point, because at this size the corner stops being a shape and becomes an easing of the edge. Below about 4px the panel step would stop registering as rounded at all and the theme would collide with the main theme's 0, so this is roughly the floor for a theme that still calls itself rounded. Two things this gives up: the agreement with axiroster's 10px frameless window clip (an app clipping its window to 10px now has visibly tighter panels at the corner - the app's number to change, not the theme's), and any trace of axiroster in the radii at all. The fold now lives entirely in the relief, the lit top edge and the hairline. Glass sits well above at 16/10/4 and the main theme at 0, so the three still read as one scale, with flat pulled close to the square end of it.
//paint: Each of the surfaces this theme paints with a gradient also restates its -paint companion, the same surface as one flat <color>, because a token holding a gradient can only ever BE a background and consumers want these fills in places that take a colour - a chart's fill, an operand of color-mix(), a border-color. See --axi-surface-paint in tokens.css for why that is a companion rather than a split. The values are not a fresh judgement: each is the midpoint of the gradient above it, the colour that gradient is a narrow spread around. Restating them is not optional for a theme that grades a surface - the companions are aliased to the surfaces in tokens.css, so a theme that grades one and forgets the other hands the gradient straight back. Flat is where the two halves read most plainly: #1a1f2e and #222838 are literally the flat values the note above has always named, and each gradient is exactly the +-4 spread around its own. --axi-surface-float-paint needs no restating for the same reason --axi-surface-float does not: it follows --axi-surface-paint, which is why tokens.css aliases it there rather than to the float. The note above used to argue the folded gradient was safe because every surface token is consumed through the background shorthand and never background-color. That was true of the package and false of its consumers: under this theme axibridge got rgb(0, 0, 0) twice and no fill at all once.
